INTRO. We were given four movies of compressible convection: a gas heated from below and cooled from above. Three are 2D, at Rayleigh numbers 10⁹, 10¹² and 10¹⁵, and one is 3D at 10⁸. The Rayleigh number says how strongly the fluid is driven; higher Ra means more turbulence. We had no simulation data, only the movies. So we read the temperature and density back from the colours, and then measured the energy spectra and other statistics from those pixels.

ROADMAP. Slide 2: the full 2D temperature spectrum, using an FFT in x and a mirror trick in z. Slide 3: the entropy of the spectrum and what the density panel tells us. Slide 4: the mean temperature profile and the thin boundary layers at the plates. Slide 5: sound waves in the movies.
spec2d:
THE QUESTION. Hot fluid rises and cold fluid sinks, making swirls of every size. How is the temperature variation shared between big and small sizes? The energy spectrum E(K) answers this: small K = big structures, large K = small structures. Step 0: the movie has only colours, so each pixel colour is matched to the colour bar in the frame to get a temperature.

THE PROBLEM. In x the box wraps around, so a plain FFT along each row is exact. In z there are walls (the two plates), so z does not wrap around, and a plain FFT in z would be wrong.

THE TRICK. (1) Subtract the background temperature line (1 − Dz) and add εz. The new field θ′ is exactly zero at the bottom plate and at the top plate. (2) Mirror trick, z → 2 − z: for 1 ≤ z ≤ 2 put −θ′(2 − z), the column reflected about the top plate with its sign flipped. Both pieces are zero at z = 1, and the ends z = 0 and z = 2 are zero too, so the 2-long column repeats with no jump and an FFT over it is exact. Because sin(nπ(2 − z)) = −sin(nπz), only sine waves sin(nπz) appear, with k_z = nπ. (Reflecting about the bottom plate, z → −z, gives the same thing. In the code this is the DST-I.) (3) FFT in x × sine series in z gives every 2D wave (kx, kz). (4) Add the energy of all waves with the same total size K (a ring in the kx–kz plane), and fit the slope at K/π = 5–15. The mean profile is left out here; it is slide 4.

READING THE FIGURE. Each line is one movie; the dashed line has slope −5/3; the grey band is the fit range K/π = 5–15.

THE NUMBERS. −1.27 (Ra 10⁹), −1.62 (Ra 10¹²), −2.27 (Ra 10¹⁵). Ra 10¹² matches −5/3, the classic turbulence result for a mixed quantity like temperature (Obukhov–Corrsin). Ra 10¹⁵ is steeper (−2.11 over K/π 10–40, close to −2); slide 3 explains why. A plain 1D FFT along x gives the same picture: −1.52, −1.59, −2.35.

SAY: "Using both directions, the temperature spectrum follows −5/3 at Ra 10¹² and becomes steeper at Ra 10¹⁵."

EXTRA. The same modes show the middle of the box is isotropic: vertical and horizontal energy are nearly equal (ratio 1.01, 1.06, 1.17). Only the plates make the whole box anisotropic.

IF ASKED "why is the 10¹² error bar so wide?": that movie holds only about 4 independent time samples. IF ASKED "is the trick reliable?": on synthetic movies the plates come back within 0.03 px and the slopes within 0.03.
entropy:
ENTROPY OF A SPECTRUM. Treat E(k) divided by the total as probabilities p_k, then compute the Shannon entropy S = −Σ p_k log₂ p_k. S = 0: all the energy is in one size. S = 7.2 bits: energy spread evenly over 150 sizes (white noise). Low S: a few big structures dominate. (A pure −5/3 spectrum gives 3.2 bits.)

THE RESULT. S falls as Ra rises: 4.44 → 3.67 → 2.82 bits in 1D, and 4.36 → 3.97 → 3.00 with the 2D rings. Each step is significant. At high Ra the temperature is held by fewer, larger structures.

WHY IS RA 10¹⁵ STEEPER? The movie also shows density ρ. For an ideal gas p = ρT, so every cold spot can be sorted. Cold and heavy = a plume (falling cold fluid). Cold and light = a vortex core (low pressure in the centre of a spinning swirl). Exactly: ln T = entropy part + pressure part. The pressure share is the part of the temperature variation that comes from vortex cores: 28% → 77% → 97%. Vortex cores have a steep spectrum, which explains the steeper slope at Ra 10¹⁵ (−2.27 in 2D). In the 3D movie it is only 7%: big long-lived vortices are a 2D effect.

THE CHECK BOX. The same split gives back the gas constants from pixels: γ − 1 = 0.29 and D = 0.48, against 0.30 and 0.50 printed on the movie. So the colour reading is correct for both T and ρ.

SAY: "As Ra rises, vortex cores take over the temperature field, the spectrum steepens and the entropy falls."
branch:
THE IDEA. Take θ′ (temperature minus the straight plate-to-plate line, as on slide 2). At each height z, average it over all pixels across the box (along x) and over all 1001 frames: one number per height. Together these give one curve against height, the mean profile Θ(z). Then write Θ(z) as a sum of sine waves sin(nπz); Eₙ = ½ aₙ² is the energy of the n-th wave (n = 1 half a wave, n = 2 one full wave, and so on). This mean profile holds 96% of all the variation. In the middle it is a straight line. Near each plate there is a thin layer (the boundary layer) where the temperature jumps.

WHY THIS GIVES k⁻². A sudden jump, written as a sine series, has coefficients that fall like 1/n, so the energy falls like 1/n². I measured the two jumps (J₀ at the bottom, J₁ at the top) from the profile, by extending the straight middle part to each plate, and put them into the formula on the slide. Nothing is fitted.

READING THE FIGURE. Left panel: the averaged profile itself for Ra 10¹², height going up. It is a straight line in the middle (dashed), and near each plate it bends back to zero in a thin layer: those are the two jumps, 0.27 ε at the bottom and 0.74 ε at the top. (All three movies: bottom 0.20–0.27 ε, top 0.74–0.79 ε.) Right panel: dots = measured energy of each sine wave. Lines = the formula's prediction from the two jumps. Ra 10¹² and 10¹⁵: the dots sit on the lines (ratio 0.98 and 1.00), and the slope is about −2.1 against −2 in theory. Ra 10⁹: the dots drop below the line, because there the boundary layers are thick enough to see in the pixels, so they are not sharp jumps. (Their thickness from the fit, 0.010–0.028, agrees in size with jump ÷ plate gradient, 0.018–0.039.)

THE SURPRISE. The jumps are 0.25 ε at the bottom and 0.75 ε at the top, in all three 2D movies, and they add up to about ε. A simple incompressible (Boussinesq) fluid would give 0.5 and 0.5. The difference is an effect of compressibility.

SAY: "The vertical spectrum is set by the two thin layers at the plates, and a formula with zero fitted numbers predicts it."
sound:
THE METHOD. (1) From slide 2, each frame splits into 2D waves, each with one strength. Follow one wave's strength through all 1001 frames (0.01 time units apart): that is a signal in time. FFT it to find how fast that wave wobbles. Slow, irregular change = drifting plumes and swirls; a clean fast oscillation = a sound wave passing. (2) Plot the power against size K and frequency. (3) A wave that always moves at one speed c makes a straight line through the origin: ω = cK. Its slope is the speed.

READING THE FIGURE. Dark = more power. A dark straight ridge runs along the dashed line. The dashed line is not a fit: it is the ideal-gas sound speed √((γ−1)T/(Dε)), computed from γ = 1.3, D = 0.5, ε = 0.1 printed on the movie and averaged over the depth: 2.09.

THE NUMBERS. Measured speed 1.93–2.08 (from both the temperature and the density panels), theory 2.09. At Ra 10¹⁵ sound waves carry 20% of the temperature variation; at 10¹² only 4%; at 10⁹ and in 3D there are none.

SAY: "The movies contain real sound waves, at the speed the gas law predicts."

CLOSE WITH THE HONEST PART. Every test that needs no fitted number passes: −5/3 at Ra 10¹², the k⁻² branch from the plates, γ and D from pixels, the isotropic middle of the box, and the sound speed. The open question is the steep slope at Ra 10¹⁵ (−2.27 in 2D): vortex cores and sound waves are the likely causes, but I have not proved which.

LIMITS IF ASKED. At Ra 10⁹ video compression limits k above about 80. The 10¹² movie holds only about 4 independent time samples. The 3D movie shows only 2 independent wall planes, each drawn twice.

IF ASKED "why does Ra 10¹² match best?": at 10⁹ the turbulence is weak, so the straight range is short; at 10¹⁵ vortex cores and sound waves change the spectrum.
